# Competitive Signal Report — Enterprise AI Platform (Wednesday, 12 August 2026)

> **Bottom line:** Competitors are focusing on expanding AI agent capabilities and partnerships, but gaps remain in true omnichannel integration and predictable cost models, presenting clear opportunities for Kore.ai's validated, full-scope platform.

### Cresta Partners for Broader CX AI Reach
**What happened —** (2026-08-11) Cresta announced a partnership with Firstsource Solutions to accelerate AI-powered customer experience transformation, aiming to enhance AI agent capabilities and customer engagement. [Morningstar](https://news.google.?oc=5)
**What it means for Kore.ai —** This partnership highlights Cresta's continued focus on expanding its reach, but it underscores their reliance on partners for broader enterprise deployment, a gap Kore.ai fills with its native omnichannel capabilities and extensive integration ecosystem.

### NICE Expands Customer Engagement with Currys
**What happened —** (2026-08-12) NICE announced that Currys has transformed its customer engagement using NICE, resulting in higher Net Promoter Score (NPS) and faster resolution times. [Business Wire](https://news.google.?oc=5)
**What it means for Kore.ai —** While NICE highlights positive customer outcomes, their focus remains on their existing CCaaS platform. Kore.ai's agentic AI platform offers a more comprehensive, AI-native approach that drives deeper automation and better TCO, rather than incremental improvements on a legacy seat-based model.

### IBM Strengthens Governance with watsonx Orchestrate
**What happened —** (2026-08-11) IBM announced new "Enforcement Tracking" capabilities for watsonx Orchestrate, designed to help organizations manage governance policies and ensure proof of compliance. [IBM](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMizAFBVV95cUxNX3hXVVpyRGtZd0lUelBCZDZrSTN0aHRGalVfcXd4bGxQQmxCMU83SlZzNGVpV2NHZTQxVFFRb2hBbFV4dkpheGlvV2x6cF8tMmJLeW9ab00zRTRYV1lOWUtMejhoUG84MjlnbzZUdXI1SzZkWUJSNnhjQ1V1UXVUUU1FRzNvZVB4WUkzSm5KcHdBODRWUEVPR0VaX3ltRHVsTDI3MWhUSG5DWkRidzlkU0JZNTNpTU1nZ2lkcjFWZDVfdkd5cHBtQm9LUVg?oc=5)
**What it means for Kore.ai —** IBM's focus on governance is a positive step, but it highlights the inherent complexity and potential for drift in LLM-based agentic systems. Kore.ai's ABL provides compile-time validation and deterministic execution, offering a more robust and inherently governed approach to agent behavior, reducing the need for complex post-hoc enforcement.

## Watch for
- Agentforce's continued push into voice and contact center, and how it integrates with third-party telephony partners.
- Parloa's expansion beyond Europe and any new analyst validation for their platform.
- Further details on IBM's "agentic control plane" strategy and its integration with third-party LLMs.

## Recommended actions
- Emphasize Kore.ai's **native omnichannel capabilities** in all voice and digital customer interactions, contrasting with partners-reliant or voice-first approaches.
- Highlight Kore.ai's **predictable cost-per-outcome model** and compile-time validation as key differentiators against consumption-based pricing and post-hoc governance.
- Reinforce Kore.ai's **leader placement in key CX conversational AI analyst evaluations** (Gartner, Forrester) as proof of platform maturity and breadth.
- Arm sales teams with specific questions that probe competitors' reliance on third-party voice infrastructure and their governance models' ability to prevent LLM drift.
